newsitem.title: UK: Fuji Bank 200 bln yen convertible expected.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Bank 200 bln yen convertible expected.

text.p: Japan's Fuji Bank plans to issue a 200 billion yen Euro-convertible bond, syndicate managers said on Friday.
Newspaper reportss said the deal had been mandated to SBC Warburg, Nomura and Yamaichi.
Officials there declined to comment, but other syndicate sources said a deal for Fuji was expected to surface within about a month.
"There has been no official announcement yet, but there is talk such a deal is in the pipeline," an equity syndicate manager here said.
In September 1995 Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi issued a $2.0 billion exchangeable bond, opening the sector for other Japanese banks as a means of raising capital.
Since then, Tokai Bank, Sumitomo Bank and Sakura Bank has also launched convertible bonds, dealers said.
"A number of Japanese banks need to raise capital, and convertible bonds are an attractive way of doing so," a trader at a European bank said.
